rationale: The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (cache dependency downloads) is supported by measured evidence: experiment batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9 shows adding an actions/cache@v4 step for ~/go/pkg/mod keyed on go.mod/go.sum reduced median elapsed time by 6.06% with identical success, and the pattern reports about 6% free / 3.4% paid VM-time reduction. This workflow's Go jobs (gofmt, golangci-lint, go-fix, go-mod-tidy, test) repeatedly resolve/download Go modules on every run but have no cache step, while go.mod and go.sum exist and CI history shows repeated successful runs, satisfying the preconditions (repeated dependency fetching measurable; cache inputs include the lockfile). No contraindication applies: the cached module content is trusted dependency state, and no equivalent cache exists in those jobs (integration-test already caches and is left unchanged). I added a Cache Go modules step after setup-go and before each check/test run in the five jobs, matching the evidence artifact exactly, preserving all build/test coverage and adding no secrets, privileged actions, permission changes, or new network access.
